title: Hamburger Kunsthalle: Masterpieces
subtitle: Twenty works about access to a figure, a landscape or a public space.
introduction:
Nana turns away from her mirror and meets the viewer's gaze. Friedrich's wanderer does the reverse: he faces the landscape and keeps his face unavailable. These two famous figures establish different terms for looking. One acknowledges a presence outside the picture; the other offers a position from which to approach a view while withholding a personal response to it.

The rest of this selection extends the question into gardens, workplaces and places of entertainment. People may be absorbed in tasks, identified by uniforms, or crowded into a performance. Landscape can conceal as much as it reveals. The guide follows what each picture makes accessible and what remains beyond its visible evidence.
visitNote: The selected works belong to the Kunsthalle’s collection, but displays and loans change. Drawings may be shown only temporarily. Use the museum’s current collection and exhibition information to check an individual work before visiting.

books.title: Concerning the Spiritual in Art
books.author: Wassily Kandinsky; translated by Michael Sadleir
books.note: Kandinsky’s discussion of colour and form gives context for the abstract and expressionist works here. Read it as one artist’s argument, then compare it with Baumeister, Beckmann and Modersohn-Becker’s very different pictures.

works.title: Nana
works.credit: Édouard Manet. Nana. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/edouard-manet/nana-1877
works.description: The mirror is no longer the woman's focus: she turns towards the viewer. At the side, the seated man is only partly admitted into the frame. Manet gives the two figures unequal visibility and makes looking an event within the dressing scene. Nana is not simply available for inspection; her outward gaze interrupts that comfortable arrangement.

works.title: Wanderer above the Sea of Fog
works.catalogueTitle: The Wanderer Above the Sea of Fog
works.credit: Caspar David Friedrich. The Wanderer Above the Sea of Fog. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The man's firm footing contrasts with the mist that hides much of the terrain. His back provides a bodily position from which to approach the view, but his expression cannot tell us how to interpret it. Friedrich joins apparent command to incomplete knowledge. Standing high does not make the landscape fully available.

works.title: Adoration of the Child
works.credit: Master Francke. Adoration of the Child. WikiArt source label: Master Francke Fair Use. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/master-francke/adoration-of-the-child
works.license: Master Francke Fair Use (WikiArt source label)
works.description: Rich colour and pattern could disperse attention across the surface. The kneeling figures bring it back towards the newborn child. Master Francke uses bodily direction to organise a setting that is also conspicuously decorative. The small central group does not have to occupy most of the panel to determine the surrounding figures' purpose.

works.title: Bluxao V
works.credit: Willi Baumeister. Bluxao V. WikiArt source label: Willi Baumeister Fair Use. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/willi-baumeister/bluxao-v-1955
works.license: Willi Baumeister Fair Use (WikiArt source label)
works.description: Bright extensions pull away from the darker central forms in several directions. Their weight and placement establish a balance that remains active against the blue ground. Baumeister permits a suggestion of a figure without requiring every part to acquire an anatomical name. Relations among colours are sufficient to sustain the arrangement.

works.title: Eve
works.credit: Henri Rousseau. Eve. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/henri-rousseau/eve-1907
works.description: Leaves and fruit form something closer to an enclosing screen than a distant garden. Rousseau separates the repeated plant shapes clearly, giving vegetation an order as conspicuous as Eve and the snake. The biblical setting is constructed through accumulation. Depth matters less than the density of a world whose parts remain individually legible.

works.title: Swift Hope
works.credit: René Magritte. Swift Hope. WikiArt source label: Rene Magritte Fair Use. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/rene-magritte/swift-hope-1928
works.license: Rene Magritte Fair Use (WikiArt source label)
works.description: The words offer names, but the nearby shapes do not obediently illustrate them. Magritte interrupts a routine agreement between reading and seeing. A label may direct attention without supplying a dependable identification. The painting is useful precisely where that agreement fails: it exposes the extra act of interpretation hidden inside apparently straightforward naming.

works.title: Amsterdam Orphan Girls in the Garden
works.credit: WikiArt. Public domain. Full source frame preserved; proportional resize and JPEG compression.
works.description: Uniform dresses and aprons establish the girls as a group, while their hands attend to separate pieces of work. Birds add less regulated movement on the ground. Liebermann allows institutional routine and garden activity to occupy the same space. Similar clothing does not make the figures identical in their actions or attention.

works.title: The Net Menders
works.credit: Max Liebermann. The Net Menders. Image credit: Max Liebermann; anagoria. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:1888_Liebermann_Die_Netzflickerinnen_anagoria.JPG. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: The shared task spreads across open ground rather than gathering around one central workstation. A standing foreground figure establishes scale, while other positions show different parts of the labour. Liebermann gives repetitive work a broad setting without converting it into a single emblematic gesture. The nets connect actions that remain individually distinct.

works.title: View from Pimonte over the Bay of Naples
works.catalogueTitle: Blick von Pimonte auf die Bucht von Neapel
works.credit: Johan Christian Dahl. Blick von Pimonte auf die Bucht von Neapel. Image credit: Johan Christian Dahl; Source credit: Photographer and uploader was Hajotthu at de.wikipedia. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Foreground rocks, trees and travellers make the distant bay measurable. Smoke rising from the volcano introduces activity into what might otherwise appear a settled prospect. Dahl holds near and far together without giving them equal detail. The broad view includes a force whose presence can be registered from a distance but not fully inspected.

works.title: Boats on the Beach
works.credit: Max Beckmann. Boats on the beach. Image credit: Max Beckmann. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Dark outlines give sails, hulls and people a comparable insistence. Beckmann compresses the beach into wedges and curves against strong areas of sand and water. The spaces between boats matter as much as individual vessels: they are where figures must fit. The shore feels constructed from interlocking shapes rather than opening freely into distance.

works.title: The Surgeon Ferdinand Sauerbruch
works.credit: WikiArt. Public domain. Full source frame preserved; proportional resize and JPEG compression.
works.description: The white coat identifies a profession without requiring an operation or an array of instruments. Against pale surroundings, the turn of the head concentrates attention on the sitter. Liebermann keeps role and likeness distinguishable. The coat tells us what kind of authority is being presented; the particular face cannot be reduced to that public sign.

works.title: The Terrace of the Hotel Louis C. Jacob
works.catalogueTitle: Die Terrasse des Hotel Louis C. Jacob in Nienstedten an der Elbe
works.credit: WikiArt. Public domain. Full source frame preserved; proportional resize and JPEG compression.
works.description: Tables, chairs and tree trunks give the terrace a repeated structure. Patches of light and shade loosen that framework as it recedes beside the river. Liebermann makes public leisure depend on an ordered space that can still accommodate separate groups. The scene's ease is supported by the arrangement rather than explained through imagined conversations.

works.title: Head of a Child
works.credit: Head of a child. WikiArt; Albrecht Dürer. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: Closed eyes and slightly parted lips establish a passing bodily state without explaining its cause. Dürer gives curling hair and smooth cheeks different kinds of marks, making the act of drawing visible alongside the face. The isolated head invites close observation. A surrounding story would add information, but it is not needed to make the study particular.

works.title: Hamburg after the Fire of 1842
works.credit: Jacob Gensler. Hamburg after the Fire of 1842. Image credit: Jacob Gensler; Source credit: ~. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The damaged city is described partly through newly open space. Surviving masonry and scattered remains frame a view that destruction has made possible. Gensler's small figures measure that exposure. The scene records more than individual ruined buildings: it shows how loss changes the relation between the foreground, the water and what can now be seen beyond.

works.title: Inside the Palm House on the Pfaueninsel
works.catalogueTitle: Inside the Palm House on the Pfaueninsel near Potsdam
works.credit: Carl Blechen. Inside the Palm House on the Pfaueninsel near Potsdam. Image credit: Carl Blechen. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Palm leaves cross the glazed building's framework, setting two kinds of structure against one another. Small figures beneath the plants make their scale apparent. Blechen's interior is both cultivated vegetation and elaborate architecture. The greenhouse does not disappear behind its contents; its visible construction helps explain the conditions under which this indoor abundance can exist.

works.title: The Twelve-Year-Old Jesus in the Temple
works.credit: Max Liebermann; Hamburger Kunsthalle, online Sammlung. Public domain. Full source frame preserved; proportional resize and JPEG compression.
works.description: A boy addresses men whose age, books and clothing suggest established authority. Their close grouping turns the religious subject into a visible exchange of speaking and listening. Liebermann makes the difference in age consequential through position and response. The scene's tension comes from who receives attention, not simply from the number of people present.

works.title: Mother and Child
works.credit: Paula Modersohn-Becker. Mother and Child. Image credit: Paula Modersohn-Becker; Source credit: Hamburger Kunsthalle, Onlinesammlung. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The pair's joined shapes make holding the central fact of the picture. Broad colour areas give the bodies weight while limiting the amount of facial explanation. Modersohn-Becker does not need a conspicuously sentimental expression to establish care. The physical relation between the larger body and the child supplies an intelligible structure on its own.

works.title: Nordic Landscape
works.credit: Johan Christian Dahl. Nordic Landscape. Image credit: Johan Christian Dahl; Source credit: Photographer and uploader was Hajotthu at de.wikipedia. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The bright distance must be reached through close woodland, fallen timber and rough ground. Dahl makes these obstacles part of the view rather than clearing them away for a pleasing prospect. Near textures and distant light require different attention. The landscape offers an opening, but the foreground continues to assert its material presence.

works.title: Old Peasant Woman
works.credit: Paula Modersohn-Becker. Old Peasant Woman. Image credit: Paula Modersohn-Becker. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: One hand supports the head while the other arm crosses the body. These substantial forms give the portrait its organisation before any interpretation of expression. Modersohn-Becker keeps the clothing dark and the face plainly stated. The supported posture can be observed without turning it into an invented diagnosis of exhaustion, resignation or the sitter's whole life.

works.title: Sea Lions in the Circus
works.credit: Max Beckmann. Sea lions in the circus. Image credit: Max Beckmann. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Hoops, animals and coloured structures compete inside the narrow format. Beckmann's heavy contours keep them readable while making the performance space feel tightly packed. Entertainment appears as an arrangement of bodies and equipment with little spare room. The scene's energy is inseparable from these restrictions rather than being a simple image of unrestricted movement.

closingSections.title: Notice the terms of access
paragraphs: Compare Nana's outward glance with the wanderer's hidden face, then consider how uniforms and professional clothing change the other portraits. This is a collection selection, not a guarantee of current display. Check availability when planning a visit around a particular work.
